AI-enabled Children Story Telling Market.verdict: Essentially the same preference convergence; broader parent ages do not establish eligible or representative households
AI-enabled Children Story Telling Market.execution: Completed the unchanged corrected 50-person survey, profiling, ranking extraction and empirical comparisons. Source/library audit passed.
findings: All 50 public rankings and all 50 extracted rationales were read. Every extracted order exactly matches the corresponding public A-E permutation.
All 50 again rank B (no AI device) first, versus 14% of human controls; none of the preference-convergence problem is resolved in this rollout.
Budget and device-format trade-offs are coherent but nearly everyone uses the same unsupervised-AI, privacy, screen-time and parent-control structure.
Parent ages broaden from the prior 34-39 cluster to 18-66, but 45 of 50 profiles still have a Practical-labelled trait and healthcare/front-office roles remain common.

At least seven public answers explicitly state there is no young child at home or that the person's children are older. These are not eligible current parents of 4-5-year-olds, despite the target population and each sampling directive saying so.
All six figures were inspected. Thematic behavioral charts are readable, but geographic distribution still uses nationality rather than residence.
The structured sampling adapter validates the plan's shape but does not guarantee that generated personas satisfy household eligibility or produce representative population coverage.
Unanimous rejection is recorded as a model output, not changed to force enthusiasm or agreement with human controls; this rollout does not isolate a causal model or prompt effect.
AI-enabled Children Story Telling Market.decision: Do not promote as a validated market simulation.

Investment Firm.execution: Completed the unchanged three-agent, twenty-step notebook. Source and library audit passed. Both professionals actually CONSULTed both Vale PDFs.
findings: The company analysis distinguishes Vale shipments from market-wide demand, management forecasts from observed results, and company analysis from portfolio suitability.
The analyst repeatedly reproduces the same labeled Q3 evidence summary rather than progressing the discussion; adviser and customer repeatedly exchange watch-list/no-trade closings.
The adviser actually delivers a written recap when requested instead of only promising it, but further nearly identical closing turns continue.

One analyst statement mislabels US$3.741 billion as Iron Ore Solutions EBITDA; the supplied PDF reports US$3.731 billion for that segment and US$3.741 billion company-wide. Later public speech correctly distinguishes them.
A changed generated cohort prevents attributing the different number of utterances or duration causally to the prompt repairs.
